Mean pairwise cosine measures average angular alignment, not dimensional collapse: balanced vectors along one axis can average near zero despite rank one; averaging also hides clusters and ignores norms. High cosine may reflect a shared offset rather than lost discriminative variation. Dimensional collapse means confinement to a low-dimensional subspace ([Jing et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.09348)). Sampled positive–negative margins depend on negative difficulty and score scale; enlarging dot-product norms can increase margins without changing ranks. Beating easy training negatives does not establish validation HR@10.

Complement cosine with singular-value spectra and effective rank, exp(−Σpᵢ log pᵢ), explicitly defining pᵢ=σᵢ/Σσⱼ; covariance-eigenvalue entropy is a different statistic ([RankMe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02885)). For NextItNet, examine item embeddings excluding padding and final nonpadding sequence features separately, reporting centered and uncentered spectra, top-component energy, coordinate variance, and norm quantiles/near-zero fractions. Keep samples and normalization consistent; centered effective rank from 200 users cannot exceed min(d,199). These are proposed structural diagnostics, not guarantees of ranking quality.

For the same 200 users/category and unchanged 99 negatives, retain per-user HR@10 indicators and compare models through gained hits, lost hits, and ΔHR=(gains−losses)/200. Report category results and their macro-average; use paired bootstrap intervals, resampling user pairs within categories, or exact McNemar tests on discordant hits. Pairing follows established retrieval-comparison practice ([Smucker et al.](https://ciir-publications.cs.umass.edu/getpdf.php?id=744)). Inspect positive ranks and margins against the tenth-highest negative, respecting evaluator ties. One changed hit equals 0.5 percentage points/category, 0.125 macro points. Fixed candidates support paired comparisons but do not establish full-catalog quality; sampled metrics can reverse model orderings ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Repeated validation selection also makes uncertainty estimates optimistic.
